title: Jesus the Christ: A Study of the Messiah and His Mission According to Holy Scriptures, Both Ancient and Modern
author: James E. Talmage
edition_analyzed: Original edition, commonly used 2011 Deseret Book edition
target_audience: Members of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (LDS Church)
General Christians interested in the life of Jesus Christ
Readers seeking in-depth doctrinal analysis of Jesus Christ’s life and mission
core_themes: The divinity and humanity of Jesus Christ
Harmony of ancient and modern scripture regarding Jesus’ life and mission
Doctrinal context for Christ’s miracles, teachings, and roles
Relationship between Jesus and God the Father
primary_purpose: To provide an in-depth, doctrinally grounded study of Jesus Christ’s life, mission, and teachings, synthesizing insights from both the Bible and uniquely Latter-day Saint scripture and perspectives, thereby strengthening faith and understanding among believers.

structure_format.organization: Chronologically organized narrative biography, divided into 42 chapters covering pre-mortal existence, mortal ministry, atonement, and post-resurrection events
features: Integration of ancient and modern revelation
Summative conclusions at the end of major narrative sections

key_concepts_lessons: Jesus Christ existed with the Father before His mortal birth and was foreordained as Savior.
The mortal life of Jesus fulfilled ancient prophecy and serves as the central event of human history.
Christ’s teachings, miracles, and interactions illustrate His dual nature as both divine and human.
The Atonement and Resurrection are presented as fulfilling God’s plan for salvation and providing hope for all mankind.
Modern revelation, as accepted by Latter-day Saints, offers additional insights into Jesus’ character and mission.
Understanding Christ’s mission requires harmonizing teachings from the Bible, Book of Mormon, Doctrine and Covenants, and Pearl of Great Price.
style_tone: Accessible to lay and scholarly audiences alike
notable_features: A seminal Latter-day Saint work, often recommended and quoted by LDS leaders
Comprehensive use of canonical LDS scripture alongside the Bible
Authoritative doctrinal interpretation from an LDS perspective
Continues to be a standard text for LDS missionaries, educators, and members
cultural_historical_context: Published in 1915 at the invitation of the First Presidency of the LDS Church and written while James E. Talmage served as an Apostle, 'Jesus the Christ' responded to early 20th-century needs for doctrinal clarification and education. It remains a pillar of LDS doctrinal literature and is unique in its synthesis of ancient and Restoration scripture regarding Jesus Christ. Its composition in the Salt Lake Temple's council room adds to its reverence and historical significance within LDS tradition.
reception_impact: Regarded as a definitive LDS doctrinal text on the life and mission of Jesus Christ
Standard reading for missionaries and seminary/institute students
Highly influential in shaping Latter-day Saint understanding and teaching about Jesus
Praised for its depth and scholarly rigor, though some non-LDS audiences may view its conclusions as specific to LDS theology
